questions.q: At cfg = 1, what does the negative prompt change?
options: Nothing, it is not even evaluated
It removes the concept at half strength
questions.answer: Nothing, it is not even evaluated
questions.why: D = D_neg + (D_pos − D_neg) · 1 = D_pos, and sampling_function skips the run.

questions.q: If positive and negative are the same text, a higher cfg
options: Changes nothing, because their difference is zero
questions.answer: Changes nothing, because their difference is zero
questions.why: Guidance is the difference. The lab's third row equals its first to every digit.

questions.q: A negative prompt is best described as
options: A list the model subtracts from the image
What fills the second branch of the CFG formula
questions.answer: What fills the second branch of the CFG formula
questions.why: There is no concept subtraction. It only changes which prediction the positive is compared with.

questions.q: What is the side effect of a negative prompt shown in the lab?
options: Samples get closer to the data
All samples are pushed outward, not only those that would have been foxes
questions.answer: All samples are pushed outward, not only those that would have been foxes
questions.why: At cfg 3 the median distance goes from 3 to 12.39, although the data sits at 3.

questions.q: Why might the same cfg feel stronger with a specific negative prompt?
options: The difference between the two predictions is larger
questions.answer: The difference between the two predictions is larger
questions.why: The lab: dog against any reaches 3.63, and dog against fox reaches 13.00, at the same cfg.
